claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have a child (or children) that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's helpful to know about Alex.

To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, are you currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. We're based in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you.

Next, I need to ask: are you or Alex subject to immigration control, or do either of you have any restrictions on your right to reside in the UK? For example, do you have any visa conditions that restrict access to public funds?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, we're not subject to any immigration control and there are no restrictions on our right to reside in the UK. We don't have any visa conditions or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Next, I need to ask: Is Alex living with you full-time, or does he spend time living with anyone else (for example, another parent or guardian)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me full-time at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. Now I need to ask: are you responsible for Alex? This means you're the one who provides for his day-to-day needs, such as food, clothing, housing, and generally looking after him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm the one who looks after him day-to-day - I provide his food, clothing, housing, everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

Just a few more questions: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you.

One final question: Does Alex have any circumstances that might affect his status as a qualifying young person? For example, is he in full-time non-advanced education or approved training, or does he have any other special circumstances? (This is typically more relevant for older children, but I want to make sure I have all the information.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He's only 8, so he's just in primary school - regular school for his age. No special circumstances or anything.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 8 years old, which means he's under 16 and qualifies as a child for Child Benefit purposes
- You are responsible for Alex and provide for his day-to-day needs
- Alex lives with you full-time in the UK
- You have no immigration restrictions that would prevent you from claiming
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. If you need help with the application process, you can apply online through the government's official channels or by post.
